The masked woman stared fixedly at me.
The mask had no mouth. There were only two thin slits open around the eyes.
"Now, you'll answer my questions, won't you?"
The thing spoke to me.
This time it wasn't the voice that spoke straight into my head like before. It was a clear, real voice.
And how eerie that voice was.
It was like the noise you hear when you fast-forward a tape.
That was what it sounded like.
Shrill, yet strangely muffled, as if it had an echo on it. It was a voice that clung horribly to my ears.
Was she waiting for my answer to what she'd just asked?
I swallowed the spit that had pooled in my mouth.{p}How should I answer?
rows.45:1660:
"Yes."
I let it out with my breath.
"Let me tell you one thing. I'll know if you lie.
So answer honestly, all right?"
I nodded.
Right now, I was seeing something no one in this world should ever see, and going through something no one should ever go through.
I couldn't shake that feeling.
The old saying kept coming back to me: leave the gods alone, and they won't curse you.{p}"You know the story, don't you? Back when this old school building was still in use, some students taking a make-up class were abandoned by their teacher."
